content: The studies summarized below provide detailed insights into the use of dolutegravir (DTG) and efavirenz (EFV) in pregnant women living with HIV, as well as their associated outcomes. These findings are derived from various clinical trials, observational studies, and case reports conducted across multiple countries. 1. DOLPHIN-2 Trial (South Africa and Uganda): This randomized, open-label trial compared DTG-based antiretroviral therapy (ART) with EFV-based ART in late-presenting pregnant women (gestational age [GA] >28–36 weeks). Women initially started on EFV-based ART and were switched to DTG if randomized to the DTG arm. As of May 2018, 130 women were enrolled (out of a planned 250), with 55 deliveries resulting in 54 live births. Among 66 women starting DTG-based ART, there were 28 deliveries and 27 live births. In the EFV group (64 women), there were 27 deliveries and 27 live births. Viral suppression and safety data were not fully clear, with one stillbirth reported in the DTG group compared to two in the EFV group. 2. ADVANCE Trial (South Africa): This ongoing randomized controlled trial (RCT) compares three first-line ART regimens in non-pregnant individuals: DTG/tenofovir alafenamide (TAF)/emtricitabine (FTC), DTG/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF)/FTC, and EFV/TDF/FTC. Pregnant participants were removed from the study drugs but followed for outcomes. As of May 2018, 20 pregnancies were reported, with 15 in the DTG arms and 5 in the EFV arm. 3. NAMSL Trial (Cameroon): This RCT compares DTG/TDF/FTC with EFV 400 mg/TDF/FTC as first-line ART in non-pregnant adults. Pregnant participants were switched to EFV 600 mg and followed for outcomes. Among 404 women enrolled, 26 pregnancies were reported, with 12 in the DTG group and 15 in the EFV group. 4. Tsepamo Study (Botswana): This large observational study captures birth outcomes in women delivering at eight government maternity wards, representing 45% of all births in Botswana. Between August 2014 and September 2017, 1,729 women started DTG-based ART during pregnancy, and 4,593 started EFV-based ART. Adverse birth outcomes, including stillbirth, preterm delivery, small-for-gestational-age infants, and neonatal death, were evaluated. 5. Grayhack et al. (USA): A retrospective cohort study of 66 HIV-positive pregnant women on DTG-based ART (28 preconception, 38 during pregnancy) reported 57 live births. No significant side effects from DTG were documented during pregnancy, and no mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HIV occurred. 6. Zash et al. (Botswana): This observational study compared birth outcomes in women starting DTG-based ART during pregnancy (November 2016–September 2017) with those starting EFV-based ART (August 2014–August 2016). Systematic neonatal surface examinations were conducted to identify major birth defects. No significant differences in adverse outcomes were reported between the groups. 7. Mulligan et al. (USA): Despite this, viral suppression was achieved in most participants, and no dose adjustments were deemed necessary. DTG readily crossed the placenta, with prolonged infant elimination observed. 8. Kobbe et al. (Germany): A case report described one HIV-positive woman on DTG postpartum who breastfed her infant. No adverse effects or MTCT were reported, and DTG levels in breast milk were consistent with therapeutic targets. 9. Schalkwijk et al. (Netherlands): An ex vivo placental perfusion study demonstrated that DTG crosses the placenta, although equilibrium between maternal and fetal circulations was not reached within three hours. This suggests potential underestimation of placental transfer in clinical settings. 10. Rahangdale et al. (USA): A retrospective cohort study of 101 HIV-positive pregnant women found that integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-based ART, including DTG, achieved faster viral suppression compared to non-INSTI regimens. Among women receiving DTG, no adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes were reported. 11. Orrell et al. (ARIA Trial): This phase 3b RCT compared DTG/abacavir (ABC)/lamivudine (3TC) with atazanavir/ritonavir (ATV/r)/TDF/FTC in non-pregnant ART-naïve women. Five pregnancies occurred in the DTG group, with one healthy term infant, two terminations, one anembryonic pregnancy, and one unknown outcome. No birth defects were reported. 12. ViiV Safety Reports: No significant safety concerns or birth defects were identified. 13. FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS): Reports of DTG use during pregnancy were reviewed, focusing on congenital, familial, and genetic disorders. No denominators were provided, and no significant safety signals were identified. 14. WHO VigiAccess Database: Adverse event reports for DTG during pregnancy were reviewed, with no denominators provided. No significant safety concerns were identified. These studies collectively provide valuable data on the safety, pharmacokinetics, and outcomes of DTG use during pregnancy. While DTG appears to be effective in achieving viral suppression, further research is needed to fully understand its safety profile, particularly regarding birth defects and long-term infant outcomes.
